Goldman Sachs reports a 119% surge in 'Other principal transactions revenues' to $4.65 billion, specifically citing 'significantly higher net gains from investments in private equities' and 'significantly lower net losses on hedges related to our relationship lending portfolio.' JPMorgan discloses that its increase in CIB principal transactions was partially offset by a 'net decrease in Corporate,' which included 'gains compared with a net loss on certain legacy private equity investments in the prior year.' Both firms highlight private equity investment performance as a key driver or offset within their principal transactions/other revenue lines, though GS reports a large net gain increase while JPM contrasts current gains against a prior-year loss in legacy positions.

sentences.text: Other principal transactions revenues in the consolidated statements of earnings were $4.65 billion for 2024, 119% higher than 2023, primarily reflecting significantly higher net gains from investments in private equities, significantly higher net gains from derivatives related to our funding activities, the impact of the sale of the Marcus loan portfolio in 2023 (including net revenues of approximately $(370) million related to the sale of substantially all of the portfolio) and significantly lower net losses on hedges related to our relationship lending portfolio.

The increase in CIB was partially offset by a net decrease in Corporate, reflecting lower revenue in Treasury and CIO, and gains compared with a net loss on certain legacy private equity investments in the prior year.
